back2basics.concept: Free Trade Agreement (FTA) and Trade Facilitation
back2basics.text: A Free Trade Agreement (FTA) is a pact between two or more countries to reduce or eliminate tariffs, import quotas, and preferences on most goods and services traded between them. Trade facilitation refers to simplifying and harmonizing international trade procedures, often through digitalisation and information exchange, to reduce costs and delays in cross-border trade.

2026-10-21-pm-266ecfee0d.deck: India and New Zealand signed a Memorandum of Cooperation (MoC) on electronic origin data exchange to facilitate bilateral trade under their Free Trade Agreement (FTA). This step enhances customs cooperation and trade facilitation, important for understanding India's trade diplomacy and digital trade mechanisms.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about the India-New Zealand MoC on Electronic Origin Data Exchange and the India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA):

2. The India-New Zealand FTA provides India duty-free access to 100% of New Zealand’s tariff lines.

mcq.trap: Statement 2 is correct but some may confuse it with other FTAs where duty-free access is partial; statement 1 is correct as per the MoC details.

body.label: Purpose of MoC
body.text: The MoC facilitates the advance electronic exchange of origin data on trade in goods between India and New Zealand, aiming to deepen customs cooperation and support trade facilitation measures.

body.label: Signatories and Date
body.text: Signed on 19 October 2026 by Shri Vivek Chaturvedi, Chairman of CBIC, and Ms. Christine Stevenson, Comptroller and Chief Executive of New Zealand Customs Service.

body.label: Digitalisation Focus
body.text: The MoC reflects a shared commitment to leverage digitalisation and enhanced information exchange for more efficient, secure, and predictable cross-border trade.

sections.heading: What is the MoC on Electronic Origin Data Exchange?

body.label: Trade Facilitation
body.text: The electronic exchange of origin data improves operational efficiency, reduces information gaps, and provides greater certainty to traders engaged in bilateral trade.

body.label: Utilisation of Trade Preferences
body.text: It supports effective utilisation of trade preferences under the FTA, ensuring benefits negotiated under the Agreement reach eligible businesses more efficiently.

body.label: Alignment with International Practices
body.text: The initiative aligns bilateral customs cooperation with evolving international practices in digitalisation, information exchange, and trade facilitation.

sections.heading: How does the MoC support the India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement?

body.label: Duty-Free Access
body.text: India gains duty-free access to 100% of New Zealand’s tariff lines, a unique feature compared to other Indian FTAs.

body.label: Sectoral Benefits
body.text: Sectors like textiles, apparel, leather, footwear, engineering goods, plastics, rubber, electronics, pharmaceuticals, agriculture, marine products, and chemicals benefit from tariff reductions or eliminations.

body.label: Investment Promotion
body.text: New Zealand commits to promoting foreign direct investment (FDI) into India aiming to increase it by US$ 20 billion within 15 years, subject to India’s economic growth.

body.label: Mobility Provisions
body.text: The FTA includes new Temporary Employment Entry visa categories, enhanced post-study work rights for Indian graduates, work rights during study, and a working holiday scheme for Indian nationals.

body.label: Protection of Sensitive Sectors
body.text: India excludes 30% of its tariff lines to protect sensitive and strategic sectors, while granting zero-duty imports on 30% of tariff lines from New Zealand.

back2basics.text: The judiciary has the power to review and supervise investigations and prosecutions to ensure they comply with legal procedures and protect fundamental rights. body.label: Alleged bribery case
body.text: The FIR was registered based on a Kerala High Court order directing the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau to act on a report by the Enforcement Directorate alleging fraudulent payments of ₹2.78 crore to Vijayan’s daughter’s company under the guise of IT consultancy.

body.label: Legal challenge
body.text: Vijayan and his family challenged the FIR registration, claiming they were not heard before the single judge’s order and that the matter should have been heard by a Division Bench as it involved a public interest litigation.

back2basics.concept: Ebola Virus Disease and Public Health Response
back2basics.text: Ebola Virus Disease is a severe, often fatal illness in humans caused by the Ebola virus. It spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids of infected persons or contaminated materials. Public health response includes rapid identification of cases, contact tracing, isolation, infection control measures, and international cooperation to prevent spread.

2026-10-21-pm-6ca47a97d1.deck: Nigeria has confirmed its first Ebola case caused by the Bundibugyo strain, with WHO assisting the country's health authorities. This development is important for understanding global epidemic management and the role of international health agencies.

body.label: First case details
body.text: Nigeria confirmed its first Ebola case caused by the Bundibugyo strain in a woman who traveled from Uganda and showed symptoms four days after arrival.

body.text: Infection prevention and control measures are being intensified at the private health facility where the patient sought care.

body.label: Coordination and support
body.text: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention activated its incident management system, with WHO providing technical assistance and essential supplies like personal protective equipment.

sections.heading: How is Nigeria responding to the Ebola case?

body.label: Regional outbreak context
body.text: The Bundibugyo strain outbreak began in the Democratic Republic of Congo in mid-May 2026, with over 9,500 cases and 4,200 deaths recorded, making it the deadliest in DRC's history.

body.label: Spread to multiple countries
body.text: Besides Nigeria, cases have been reported in Uganda, Kenya, and the Netherlands linked to the DRC outbreak.

body.label: No vaccine availability
body.text: Currently, there is no vaccine to treat the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus, increasing the importance of containment and surveillance.

back2basics.text: Monsoon refers to the seasonal wind pattern bringing heavy rains, critical for agriculture but also causing floods and health risks. Disaster management involves preparedness, response, and mitigation strategies to reduce the impact of natural calamities like floods and epidemics during monsoon seasons.

2026-10-21-pm-bdc6a8f9aa.deck: With the Northeast monsoon arriving, Tamil Nadu's Health Minister has directed officials to ensure uninterrupted medical services and hospital preparedness. This is crucial for managing disease spread and health emergencies during the monsoon season.

body.label: Hospital readiness
body.text: All government hospitals, primary health centres, urban primary health centres, health sub-centres, and vaccine cold chain centres in vulnerable districts are instructed to be fully prepared.

body.label: Focus on vulnerable areas
body.text: Priority is given to districts prone to flooding and heavy rainfall such as Chennai, Tiruvallur, Kancheepuram, and coastal districts like Nagapattinam and Kanniyakumari.

body.label: Advance evacuation plans
body.text: Healthcare facilities in low-lying, riverbank, and coastal areas must develop evacuation plans and patient transfer protocols to safer hospitals.

body.label: Infrastructure protection
body.text: Blood banks, vaccination centres, drug warehouses, and critical electrical infrastructure are to be located at elevated sites safe from flooding.

body.label: Medical resources and teams
body.text: Adequate medical teams, mobile units, ambulances, and emergency stocks including oxygen, medicines, ventilators, and anti-snake venom must be maintained for at least seven days.

sections.heading: What measures has Tamil Nadu taken for monsoon health preparedness?

body.label: Disease surveillance
body.text: Post-rain, surveillance is strengthened to detect diseases like dengue, leptospirosis, chikungunya, and acute diarrhoeal diseases early for prompt treatment.

body.label: Sanitation and water management
body.text: Hospital drains, sewage pipelines, and toilets are cleaned to prevent waterlogging, and pumps are kept ready to drain water from low-lying areas.

body.label: Special care for vulnerable groups
body.text: Pregnant women nearing delivery are advised to avoid flood-prone areas and seek medical advice to reduce risks.

sections.heading: How is disease prevention and surveillance managed during monsoon?

body.label: Inter-department coordination
body.text: The Health Department coordinates with Tamil Nadu Electricity Board and Public Works Department to ensure transformers and critical infrastructure remain operational.

body.label: Medical camps and relief centres
body.text: Medical camps are conducted in flood-affected areas with coordination from district administration and local bodies, and medical teams are stationed at flood relief centres.

body.label: Essential personnel engagement
body.text: Electricians, plumbers, lift operators, and sanitation workers are engaged round-the-clock to maintain hospital facilities and emergency equipment.

sections.heading: What coordination and logistical steps support monsoon health preparedness?
